ei.title: Chapter 3-08: The Quest for Certainty in Knowledge
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, justified by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This reflects the philosophical quest for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who refused to accept anything that he could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take priority over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently misled him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not conform to reason, it was likely that they were in error.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① justifying → justified
det.analysis:
✅ ① justifying — 원문은 justified. knowledge, justified by evidence(수동 분사구문: 증거에 의해 정당화된)에서 과거분사 필요. justifying(능동)이면 '정당화하는'으로 의미 부적절 ←정답
❌ ② certainty — 전치사 for 뒤 명사 certainty 적절
❌ ③ self-evident — 형용사로 propositions 수식 적절
❌ ④ conform — did not conform to(동사원형, did+원형) 적절
det.tip: justified by(~에 의해 정당화된, 수동) ≠ justifying(정당화하는, 능동)

det.korean: misled(오도했다) → enlightened(계몽했다)로 바꾸면 감각 불신의 맥락과 정반대
det.analysis:
❌ ① proven — 입증된 지식, 원문 일치
❌ ② quest — 확실성에 대한 탐구, 원문 일치
✅ ③ enlightened — 원문은 misled. 데카르트는 감각이 자주 자신을 '오도했다'고 인식. enlightened(계몽했다)로 바꾸면 정반대 ←정답
❌ ④ error — 오류 상태(were in error) 원문 일치

det.korean: conform(부합하다) → appeal(호소하다)로 바꾸면 문맥 왜곡

❌ ③ reason — 이성에 부합하는지의 기준, 원문 일치

questions.passage: Knowledge, for science, aims to be proven knowledge, justified by evidence and reason. Nothing is accepted as true unless it has been proved to be so, or there are good reasons to believe that it will be at some point in the future. This reflects the philosophical quest for certainty that goes back to René Descartes, who refused to accept anything that <u>He</u> could not know for certain to be true. He hoped to base all knowledge on self-evident propositions, and thought that reason should take priority over observation. Descartes was aware that his senses frequently misled him. The implication of this — a view which had a long history, prior to the rise of science — was that, if the evidence of our senses did not conform to reason, it was likely that they were in error.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 He가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: He = René Descartes. 바로 앞에서 데카르트를 소개한 뒤 He hoped to base...
det.analysis:
❌ ① 지식은 사물 → He(인칭) 불가
❌ ② 증거를 제시한 과학자 언급 없음
❌ ③ 감각 경험의 대상은 사물
✅ ④ René Descartes, who refused... → He hoped to base ←정답
det.tip: René Descartes → He(인칭대명사)

det.korean: they = our senses. 마지막 문장에서 the evidence of our senses... they were in error
det.analysis:

det.tip: the evidence of our senses... they(= our senses) were in error
